record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Control the correlations at the Kosterlitz-Thouless transition.

evidence.quote: Control the correlations at the KT transition.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the two-dimensional classical XY model on the square lattice $\mathbb{Z}^2$: to each site $x\in\mathbb{Z}^2$ assign a spin $\sigma_x = (\cos\theta_x,\sin\theta_x)\in S^1$, and define the formal Hamiltonian
$$H(\sigma) = -\sum_{\{x,y\}:\,|x-y|=1} \sigma_x\cdot\sigma_y = -\sum_{\{x,y\}:\,|x-y|=1}\cos(\theta_x-\theta_y).$$
For inverse temperature $\beta>0$ let $\langle\,\cdot\,\rangle_\beta$ denote the corresponding infinite-volume Gibbs measure (obtained as a limit of finite-volume measures with free or periodic boundary conditions). It is known (Fröhlich–Spencer, McBryan–Spencer) that there exists a critical inverse temperature $\beta_{\mathrm{KT}}\in(0,\infty)$ such that:
- for $\beta<\beta_{\mathrm{KT}}$, the two-point function decays exponentially: $\langle \sigma_0\cdot\sigma_x\rangle_\beta \le C(\beta) e^{-c(\beta)|x|}$;
- for $\beta>\beta_{\mathrm{KT}}$, the two-point function decays polynomially: $c_1(\beta)|x|^{-\eta(\beta)} \le \langle \sigma_0\cdot\sigma_x\rangle_\beta \le c_2(\beta)|x|^{-\eta'(\beta)}$ for some exponents $0<\eta'(\beta)\le \eta(\beta)$.

Provide a rigorous control of the two-point correlation function $\langle \sigma_0\cdot\sigma_x\rangle_{\beta_{\mathrm{KT}}}$ exactly at the Kosterlitz–Thouless transition point $\beta=\beta_{\mathrm{KT}}$, including the precise asymptotic decay rate (e.g., the exponent and possible logarithmic corrections) as $|x|\to\infty$.
artifact.status_search_result: The two-phase picture of the planar XY model is rigorously established (Fröhlich–Spencer 1981; recent elementary proofs by van Engelenburg–Lis and others give a power-law lower bound at low temperature). However, a sharp rigorous control of correlations precisely at the KT transition point — including the conjectured critical exponent and logarithmic corrections — remains an open problem; Wikipedia explicitly notes the transition "is not completely understood" rigorously.

status_evidence.title: Berezinskii–Kosterlitz–Thouless transition - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Rigorously the transition is not completely understood, but the existence of two phases was proved by McBryan & Spencer (1977) and Fröhlich & Spencer (1981).
status_evidence.claim: Behavior at the KT transition itself is not rigorously controlled.

status_evidence.title: An Elementary Proof of Phase Transition in the Planar XY Model
status_evidence.snippet: A power-law lower bound on the two-point function of the planar XY spin model at low temperatures.
status_evidence.claim: Recent results give power-law bounds in the low-temperature phase, but not at the transition.
